topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary. Its contents spill out when it is broken.
topics.operation: Open a chest to store items. Two compatible adjacent chests can join into a large chest. Keep the lid clear so it can open.
topics.storage: A single chest holds 27 stacks; a double chest holds 54. Items stay in the placed chest, and spill out when it is broken.
topics.redstone: Hoppers can insert and remove chest items. A comparator reads how full the chest is; powering an ordinary chest does not lock its lid.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary. Its contents spill out when it is broken.
topics.operation: A trapped chest stores items like a chest but emits redstone power while players have it open.
topics.storage: A single trapped chest has 27 slots. It only joins with another trapped chest, not an ordinary chest.
topics.redstone: Opening a trapped chest produces a signal based on how many players are viewing it. A comparator can separately measure its inventory fullness.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary. Its contents spill out when it is broken.
topics.operation: Use a barrel for storage where a chest lid would be blocked. A barrel can still open with a solid block above it. It is also a fisherman job-site block.
topics.storage: A barrel has 27 inventory slots. Adjacent barrels remain separate rather than combining.
topics.redstone: Hoppers can insert and remove items. A comparator measures inventory fullness; redstone power does not lock the barrel.

topics.mining: Break a shulker box by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. It drops as a box item with its inventory still inside. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place a shulker box to access it, then break it to carry the stored items. Leave room on its opening side for the lid.
topics.storage: Shulker boxes have 27 slots and retain contents when broken. You cannot put a shulker box inside another shulker box.
topics.redstone: Hoppers can transfer items into and out of placed shulker boxes. Comparators can read their inventory fullness.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the block and its contents. Without a pickaxe, only the contents drop.
topics.operation: A hopper collects and moves items automatically. It collects loose items above it, pulls items from a container above it, and transfers items into the container its spout points toward. Powering it with redstone locks its transfers. Sneak while placing it against a container to aim the spout.
topics.storage: A hopper has 5 slots. It pulls from above and pushes toward its output; pointing it upward does not make it push upward.
topics.redstone: Powering a hopper locks its own collection and transfer operations. It works automatically when unpowered; power is used to stop it, not start it.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the block and its contents. Without a pickaxe, only the contents drop.
topics.operation: A dispenser uses supported items: it can fire arrows, place water from a bucket, equip armor and perform other item-specific actions. Unsupported items are ejected as item entities.
topics.storage: This device has 9 slots. Each activation selects an occupied slot; fill the slots with the items your mechanism needs.
topics.redstone: A new redstone activation triggers one item action. Continuous power does not repeatedly dispense; use repeated pulses for repeated actions.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the block and its contents. Without a pickaxe, only the contents drop.
topics.operation: A dropper ejects an item as an item entity, or transfers it into an inventory directly in front of its output. It does not fire arrows or use buckets like a dispenser.
topics.storage: This device has 9 slots. Each activation selects an occupied slot; fill the slots with the items your mechanism needs.
topics.redstone: A new redstone activation triggers one item action. Continuous power does not repeatedly dispense; use repeated pulses for repeated actions.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the block and its contents. Without a pickaxe, only the contents drop.
topics.operation: A furnace smelts ores and materials and cooks food. Put the input in the top slot, valid fuel below and take the finished output.
topics.storage: The three slots hold input, fuel and output. Outputs must have room before processing can continue.
topics.redstone: A hopper above inserts input, a hopper from the side inserts fuel, and a hopper below extracts output. A comparator can measure the inventory; the block does not require redstone power to run.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the block and its contents. Without a pickaxe, only the contents drop.
topics.operation: A blast furnace smelts supported ores, raw metals and metal equipment faster than a furnace. It does not cook food or smelt every furnace recipe. It is an armorer job-site block.
topics.storage: The three slots hold input, fuel and output. Outputs must have room before processing can continue.
topics.redstone: A hopper above inserts input, a hopper from the side inserts fuel, and a hopper below extracts output. A comparator can measure the inventory; the block does not require redstone power to run.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect the block and its contents. Without a pickaxe, only the contents drop.
topics.operation: A smoker cooks supported foods faster than a furnace. It does not smelt ores. It is a butcher job-site block.
topics.storage: The three slots hold input, fuel and output. Outputs must have room before processing can continue.
topics.redstone: A hopper above inserts input, a hopper from the side inserts fuel, and a hopper below extracts output. A comparator can measure the inventory; the block does not require redstone power to run.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use a crafting table to access recipes that need more than your small inventory crafting area. Choose a recipe and supply the ingredients.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use a smithing table with the appropriate smithing template, equipment and material for an upgrade or armor trim. It is also the toolsmith job-site block.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use a cartography table with a map and the appropriate material to expand, clone or lock a map. It is also the cartographer job-site block.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Put a banner and dye into a loom, then choose a pattern. Some designs also require a banner pattern item. It is the shepherd job-site block.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: A fletching table is a fletcher job-site block. It currently has no player crafting interface; use ordinary crafting recipes to make arrows.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use a grindstone to repair matching items or remove ordinary enchantments for some experience. It does not remove curses. It is also the weaponsmith job-site block.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Choose a supported stone or masonry input in a stonecutter, then select its output variant. It is also the mason job-site block.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use lapis lazuli and experience levels to enchant a supported item. Up to 15 properly placed bookshelves unlock the highest offers; leave the gap between table and shelves unobstructed.

topics.mining: Break a brewing stand by hand or with a tool to collect it and its contents; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Put bottles in a brewing stand, supply blaze powder as fuel, and add the appropriate ingredient. Nether wart makes awkward potions for many potion recipes. It is the cleric job-site block.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary. Stored compost is lost; the block drops empty.
topics.operation: Add compostable plants or foods until the composter fills and produces bone meal. Different inputs have different success chances. It is the farmer job-site block.
topics.redstone: A comparator reads the compost level. A hopper above can insert compostable items; a hopper below can collect finished bone meal.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Place a book and quill or written book on a lectern for players to read. It is also the librarian job-site block.
topics.redstone: A comparator can read the current page of a book on a lectern. Turning pages also produces a brief redstone pulse.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Insert a music disc to play its recording; interact to remove the disc. The music depends on the disc, not on redstone signal strength.
topics.redstone: A playing jukebox produces redstone output. A comparator identifies the inserted disc by signal strength; it is not a volume control.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use the note block to change its pitch. A redstone activation plays its note. The block beneath controls the instrument; leave air above so it can play.
topics.redstone: A new redstone activation plays the selected note if the space above is clear. Continuous power does not play the note repeatedly.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use an anvil to rename items, repair with compatible materials or combine items and enchantments. These actions cost experience and repeated work can become too expensive.
topics.gravity: Anvils fall when unsupported and can hurt entities below. Anvils can become damaged through use or falling and eventually break.

topics.mining: A crafter drops itself by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. Stored items also drop.
topics.operation: Put ingredients in a crafter, disable slots you do not want filled, and send a redstone pulse to craft the matching recipe. The output is sent out its front.
topics.storage: A crafter has 9 ingredient slots; individual slots can be disabled to guide automated filling.
topics.redstone: Each new redstone activation attempts one craft. A comparator reports the number of occupied or disabled slots, not ordinary container fullness.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Cauldrons can hold water, lava or powder snow. Water cauldrons can wash compatible dyed items. You can also store potions and dye water for compatible coloring actions.
topics.redstone: A comparator can read a cauldron fill level. A cauldron is not a general item inventory and cannot be emptied with a hopper.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Point the observer face with the eyes toward the block you want to watch. The red-dot side is the redstone output.
topics.redstone: An observer produces a short pulse when it detects a relevant change in the block in front. Its output comes from the opposite side. Detection depends on the kind of block update, so it does not detect every imaginable change.

topics.mining: Pistons drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Power a piston to push movable blocks in front of its face. A sticky piston can also pull a suitable block back when it retracts. Some blocks cannot be moved.
topics.redstone: A piston extends while powered and retracts when power is removed. It can push at most 12 movable blocks; connected slime or honey arrangements still have to respect this limit.

topics.mining: A comparator drops as a comparator item when broken by hand or with any tool. Powered and unpowered forms are not different collectible items.
topics.operation: A comparator can read supported container fullness and compare or subtract side-input signal strengths. Use it to switch between comparison and subtraction mode.
topics.redstone: In comparison mode it passes the rear strength if neither side input is stronger. In subtraction mode it outputs rear strength minus the stronger side input, with a minimum of zero.

topics.mining: A repeater drops as a repeater item when broken by hand or with any tool. Powered and unpowered forms are not different collectible items.
topics.operation: Use a repeater to extend a redstone line, make power travel one way and add an adjustable delay.
topics.redstone: A repeater restores an incoming signal to full strength. Interact to select one of four delays. A powered repeater or comparator pointing into its side can lock its current output.

topics.mining: Daylight detectors drop themselves by hand or with any tool; an axe is fastest. An inverted detector drops a regular detector item.
topics.operation: Place a daylight detector where it can receive sky light. Interact with it to switch between ordinary and inverted operation.
topics.redstone: A daylight detector outputs a varying signal based on daylight. Inverted mode is useful for night-controlled circuits. Covering the detector or changing the weather can affect output.

topics.mining: Levers drop themselves by hand or with any tool.
topics.operation: Use a lever to toggle redstone power on and off. It stays in the selected position until used again.
topics.redstone: An on lever supplies strength 15. An off lever supplies no power. Unlike a button, it does not automatically spring back.

topics.mining: Redstone lamps drop themselves by hand or with any tool. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use a redstone lamp as a light controlled by a redstone circuit.
topics.redstone: A redstone lamp lights while powered and goes dark after power is removed; it does not toggle permanently on each pulse like a copper bulb.

topics.mining: Break a redstone torch by hand or with any tool to collect the torch item.
topics.operation: A redstone torch is a small power source that can also invert a signal. It turns off when the block it is attached to receives power.
topics.redstone: A lit redstone torch powers nearby compatible components. Rapid repeated switching can burn it out temporarily; it is not an unlimited-speed clock.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Press a wooden button for a temporary redstone signal. Arrows can also hold a wooden button active.
topics.redstone: A wooden button emits power briefly after being pressed, then resets. An arrow lodged against it keeps it activated until the arrow leaves.

topics.mining: Stone and polished blackstone buttons drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Press a stone button for a short redstone pulse. Arrows do not activate it.
topics.redstone: A stone button produces a temporary signal and resets automatically. Use a lever if you need power to stay on.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: A wooden pressure plate detects entities on it, including dropped items. Use it for a floor trigger.
topics.redstone: While an entity is pressing it, a wooden pressure plate emits full-strength power. It turns off when no longer pressed.

topics.mining: Stone pressure plates drop themselves by hand or with a tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: A stone pressure plate detects players and mobs standing on it; dropped items do not trigger it.
topics.redstone: A stone pressure plate supplies full-strength power while a player or mob presses it, then resets.

topics.mining: Weighted pressure plates drop themselves when broken by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Weighted pressure plates detect entities and vary their signal with the number present. Light gold plates reach strong signals with fewer entities than heavy iron plates.
topics.redstone: The signal depends on entity count rather than simply being on or off. Both dropped item entities and living entities can contribute.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Open or close a wooden door by hand or with redstone power. Hard-mode zombies can break susceptible wooden doors.
topics.redstone: Redstone power opens the door; removing power closes it. Wooden doors can also be operated directly by hand.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Open or close a wooden trapdoor by hand or with redstone. It changes between a flat cover and an upright panel.
topics.redstone: Redstone power opens the trapdoor; removing power closes it. You can also operate wooden trapdoors by hand.

topics.mining: Break this block by hand or with any tool to collect it; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Open a fence gate by hand or with redstone to make a passage in a fence. Closed gates stop ordinary walking passage.
topics.redstone: Power opens a fence gate and removing power closes it. Gates can also be operated directly by hand.

topics.mining: An iron door drops itself when broken by hand or with a tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: An iron door needs redstone control, such as a button, lever or pressure plate. It cannot be opened directly by hand.
topics.redstone: Power opens an iron door; removing power closes it. Use a button or lever beside the door for player access.

topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect this block. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary.
topics.operation: Use redstone to open and close an iron trapdoor. It cannot be operated directly by hand.
topics.redstone: Power opens the iron trapdoor; removing power closes it.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect a copper chest. A weaker tool drops only its contents.
topics.operation: Copper chests store items and serve as pickup sources for copper golems that sort items into other chests. Leave opening space above the lid.
topics.redstone: Hoppers can transfer items. A comparator can read inventory fullness.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes through exposed, weathered and oxidized stages. Apply honeycomb to preserve the stage, or use an axe to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time. Sneak while using the axe on a copper chest so you scrape it instead of opening it.
topics.storage: A single copper chest has 27 slots; a large copper chest has 54. Copper golems can take items from copper chests for sorting.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect a copper chest. A weaker tool drops only its contents.
topics.operation: Copper chests store items and serve as pickup sources for copper golems that sort items into other chests. Leave opening space above the lid.
topics.redstone: Hoppers can transfer items. A comparator can read inventory fullness.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper stays at its current oxidation stage. Use an axe to remove wax, then use the axe again to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time. Sneak while using the axe on a copper chest so you scrape it instead of opening it.
topics.storage: A single copper chest has 27 slots; a large copper chest has 54. Copper golems can take items from copper chests for sorting.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect the copper bulb; weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: A copper bulb is a toggleable light. Its brightness decreases as it oxidizes. Waxing preserves its current oxidation stage.
topics.redstone: Each new power activation toggles the bulb between lit and unlit. It keeps that state after power is removed. A comparator can detect whether it is lit.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes through exposed, weathered and oxidized stages. Apply honeycomb to preserve the stage, or use an axe to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect the copper bulb; weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: A copper bulb is a toggleable light. Its brightness decreases as it oxidizes. Waxing preserves its current oxidation stage.
topics.redstone: Each new power activation toggles the bulb between lit and unlit. It keeps that state after power is removed. A comparator can detect whether it is lit.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper stays at its current oxidation stage. Use an axe to remove wax, then use the axe again to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Copper doors drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Copper doors can be opened by hand as well as with redstone power. They are not redstone-only like iron doors.
topics.redstone: Power opens the copper door; removing power closes it. Manual use also works.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes through exposed, weathered and oxidized stages. Apply honeycomb to preserve the stage, or use an axe to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Copper doors drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Copper doors can be opened by hand as well as with redstone power. They are not redstone-only like iron doors.
topics.redstone: Power opens the copper door; removing power closes it. Manual use also works.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper stays at its current oxidation stage. Use an axe to remove wax, then use the axe again to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect the copper trapdoor; weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: Copper trapdoors can be opened by hand or with redstone, unlike iron trapdoors.
topics.redstone: Power opens the copper trapdoor; removing power closes it. Manual use also works.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes through exposed, weathered and oxidized stages. Apply honeycomb to preserve the stage, or use an axe to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect the copper trapdoor; weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: Copper trapdoors can be opened by hand or with redstone, unlike iron trapdoors.
topics.redstone: Power opens the copper trapdoor; removing power closes it. Manual use also works.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper stays at its current oxidation stage. Use an axe to remove wax, then use the axe again to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Copper lanterns drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Place or hang a copper lantern as a light source. It does not need redstone power.
topics.redstone: Redstone does not switch a copper lantern on and off. Use a copper bulb for a toggled light.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes through exposed, weathered and oxidized stages. Apply honeycomb to preserve the stage, or use an axe to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Copper lanterns drop themselves by hand or with any tool; a pickaxe is fastest.
topics.operation: Place or hang a copper lantern as a light source. It does not need redstone power.
topics.redstone: Redstone does not switch a copper lantern on and off. Use a copper bulb for a toggled light.
topics.oxidation: Waxed copper stays at its current oxidation stage. Use an axe to remove wax, then use the axe again to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.mining: Use a stone pickaxe or better to collect a copper grate; weaker tools drop nothing.
topics.operation: Copper grates are open-looking decorative building blocks. They can be waterlogged.
topics.redstone: A copper grate does not conduct redstone like an ordinary opaque solid block.
topics.oxidation: Unwaxed copper oxidizes through exposed, weathered and oxidized stages. Apply honeycomb to preserve the stage, or use an axe to scrape oxidation back one stage at a time.

topics.operation: Copper grates are open-looking decorative building blocks. They can be waterlogged.
topics.redstone: A copper grate does not conduct redstone like an ordinary opaque solid block.
